o1.biggest_strength: It catches the in-app checkout bug as a ship-now fix, sizes the money well, and then ranks tests around the real customer doubts: delivery, size, firmness, EMI, and trust.
o1.biggest_mistake: The test plan needs a cleaner experiment design after the checkout fix. Some sizing is based on the old baseline, and the two-at-once schedule could create interaction issues unless set up as a proper factorial test.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Refresh the baselines after the in-app fix, tighten the sample-size/MDE maths for each metric, and make the parallel-test setup safer and easier for the team to run.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives the right first call: fix the broken in-app checkout before testing, with a clear profit range. It also has smart reasoning, especially that delivery-date visibility may reduce add-to-cart but still lift orders.
o2.biggest_mistake: Some detectable-effect numbers for the two-week add-to-cart tests look too optimistic, and it misses a plain firmness test even though firmness is the second-biggest chat topic.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Correct the MDE maths, avoid invented calendar dates unless confirmed, and replace either the hero-image or reviews test with a stronger firmness-and-trial clarity test.

reason: I would rather use Output 1 because it maps more directly to our page problems and customer worries, especially size and firmness. Output 2 is very strong, but the sample-size issues and missing firmness test make me trust it a little less.
